item.title: AI Offense is Not Noclip Mode
item.description: <p>AI doesn't let attackers walk through walls, but it makes finding the cracks more efficient. In this blog, we cut through the hype and explain what AI-driven offense really looks like and why hard controls still work.</p>

item.title: We've Seen This Movie: The OT/IT Technology Divide
item.description: <p>Manufacturing knows what happens when IT and OT divide; AI governance is an unexpected chance to do it differently. In this blog, we walk through a unified governance model that bridges both before bad habits set in.</p>

item.title: SpooNMAP Grows Up: Findings, Local LLM Detection, and a Whole Lot Less Waiting
item.description: <p>SpooNMAP used to hand you a list of open ports; the latest update tells you which ones actually matter. In this blog, we detail the new automated findings reporting, LLM detection, and performance improvements.</p>

item.title: waf-fu, or Some Log Replay Nonsense
item.description: <p>AWS WAF logs are keeping receipts, including your session tokens. In this blog, we walk through the risk of default WAF logging configurations and the tool built to pull, analyze, and replay what gets left behind.</p>

item.title: LLMHaxor Update
item.description: <p>Most LLM testing tools require setup, paid access, or internet; LLMHaxor requires none of that. In this blog, we walk through the latest update, including a new WebSocket adapter for modern streaming LLM applications.</p>

item.title: So… You Found AWS Access Keys (Part 1)
item.description: <p>The AWS access keys are in hand... now what? In Part 1 of this blog series, we break down AWS credential types, where to find them, and how to validate and use them during a security engagement.</p>

item.title: Unpacking a laZzzy Donut
item.description: <p>Six stages. Multiple encryption layers. One static analysis. In this blog, we unpack a multi-stage malware loader combining Python obfuscation, Donut shellcode, and laZzzy PE encryption, without executing the payload.</p>

item.title: What's New in hate_crack Since 2.0
item.description: <p>You thought you knew hate_crack 👀 Well, version 2.0 changed that. In Part 1 of this latest blog series, we go through 13 new attack methods, menu restructuring, and local LLM integration.</p>

item.title: HashcatRosetta: Reading the Rosetta Stone of Password Cracking
item.description: <p>Meet HashcatRosetta—the Hashcat rule decoder you didn't know you needed. In Part 2 of this blog series, we go through how it translates, analyzes, and optimizes rule files to maximize cracking efficiency.</p>

item.title: Logging is a Discipline, Not a Switch
item.description: <p>Logging isn't a switch to flip; it's something to tune and maintain. In this blog, we outline a four-step Active Directory logging framework covering log sizing, audit policies, detection goals, and gap analysis.</p>
